response.text:
Recent work supports attribution probes but cautions against equating gradient decay with memory failure. [ExUA (SIGIR 2024)](https://www.amazon.science/publications/explainable-uncertainty-attribution-for-sequential-recommendation) uses gradient saliency to attribute recommendation uncertainty to historical interactions. [Johnston et al. (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608024008165) find vanishing/exploding gradients have limited explanatory power for long-term dependency learning. Earlier [gate analysis](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/26117) explains why saturation complicates learning long timescales; saturation alone therefore cannot establish harmful forgetting. Gate direction and the implemented GRU update convention matter.

A [2026 sequential-attribution benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201) reports strong faithfulness and robustness for Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP, but studies CNN/Transformer backbones and evaluates through a separately trained masking-robust probe. Its findings do not directly validate GRU diagnostics or same-network intervention faithfulness. For this task, use attribution methods as hypotheses and test them on the frozen category model; no additional fitted predictor is necessary.

Suggested diagnostic design: record update/reset gate distributions and saturation fractions over valid timesteps; measure target-versus-negative score-margin gradients with respect to historical embeddings and recurrent states by lag. Estimate an operational memory horizon through prefix truncation and controlled history replacements. Validate attribution by intervening on highly attributed versus random and low-attribution positions, matching intervention count and lag; report margin changes and rank changes on identical candidates. Repeat with multiple replacement baselines to expose masking artifacts. Connect gate patterns to failures only when matched internal-state or gate interventions change the same model’s ranking. These are proposed probes, not established causal conclusions: recency sensitivity measures model dependence, not the user’s current intent.
